title: Optimal N-of-1 Assignment for Adjacent Effects with Many Unknown Carryover Lags
banked_reason: The field-tier all-K phase claim remains priority-uncertain because CarvalhoClark1983 says that its finite tables yield conclusions about the general binary-autocorrelation class, yet its theorem text and the consequences relevant to the proposed fifth-lag projection have not been inspected.
gap_reasons: The field-tier all-K phase claim remains priority-uncertain because CarvalhoClark1983 says that its finite tables yield conclusions about the general binary-autocorrelation class, yet its theorem text and the consequences relevant to the proposed fifth-lag projection have not been inspected.
proof_attempt_summary: Presolve supplied explicit K=3 primal/dual certificates and a K=4 attainment transition; discovery then broadened this into an all-finite-K nuisance-lag phase theorem and sharpened the headline to an explicit K>=6 infinite tail. No soundness or structural defect was found, but every formulation still depended on a fifth-lag certificate whose priority could not be assessed without the inaccessible Carvalho–Clark (1983) theorem text. Re-raise after authoritative source access resolves that dependency, or after new mathematics genuinely severs the infinite-family theorem from the finite certificate.
tldr: How does fitting arbitrarily many unknown carryover lags change the best assignment for a weighted adjacent N-of-1 effect? For every finite K at least six, the proposed intercept-centered phase theorem says the three-lag precision is attainable exactly when \(b\le1/2\), with a mixing protocol below the boundary, and suffers a strict loss for every \(b>1/2\). Separate credited finite-dimensional corollaries give the three-lag closed form, the four-lag unattained boundary at \(b=1\), the fifth-lag base obstruction, structured-design comparisons, and finite schedules approaching the four-lag boundary.
gap: The classical binary-autocorrelation tables advertised only through dimension five can give finite geometry but cannot state or subsume a result quantified over every finite K at least six. Guo–Liang 2026 solves homogeneous random-switch and equal-block cycle subclasses, not the unrestricted centered-information phase in an unbounded nuisance-lag family.
fill: Prove the K at least six phase by projecting a fifth-lag switch-event certificate for strict loss and constructing dimer/Markov attainers in every low-weight dimension. Present all K at most five results as credited finite corollaries, with no novelty inference from inaccessible tables.
